title: Illustrated rosemary focaccia
description: An image-led, safety-conscious recipe fixture that associates each visual with its cooking step.
content: Illustrated rosemary focaccia recipe with ingredients, method, food safety, storage, and provenance.

metadata.subtitle: A practical image-forward recipe fixture with attached step visuals.

blocks.title: Golden rosemary focaccia
blocks.subtitle: A crisp-edged, olive-oil-rich bread for a shared lunch. The visual sequence stays beside the work it explains.

media.alt: Golden rosemary focaccia in a dark baking pan
media.credit: Synthetic fixture illustration generated for Cognis visual QA

checklist.title: Clean tea towel or reusable cover

blocks.title: Timing
blocks.content: Allow 90 minutes for the first rise. The dough must look doubled and airy before you pan it.

blocks.title: Method
blocks.subtitle: Four numbered steps with a figure immediately after the action it shows.

items.title: Make the dough
items.content: Mix flour, salt, yeast, water, and 30 ml oil until no dry flour remains.

items.title: Let it rise
items.content: Cover the bowl. Leave it at room temperature until doubled, about 90 minutes.

blocks.alt: Bowl of wet focaccia dough with a cover beside it
blocks.caption: After mixing, the dough is loose. Its first rise supplies structure and flavor.
blocks.credit: Synthetic fixture illustration generated for Cognis visual QA

items.title: Dimple the dough
items.content: Oil the pan, stretch in the dough, then press deep dimples with oiled fingertips. Add rosemary, salt, and tomatoes.

items.title: Bake until deeply golden
items.content: Bake at 220 °C for 20–22 minutes. Cool in the pan for 10 minutes before slicing.

blocks.alt: Dimpled focaccia dough with rosemary going into a hot oven
blocks.caption: The dimples hold olive oil and protect the rosemary from scorching.
blocks.credit: Synthetic fixture illustration generated for Cognis visual QA

blocks.title: If the dough resists stretching
blocks.content: Rest it for 10 minutes, then stretch again. Do not add extra flour; it makes the crumb dry.

blocks.title: If the top browns too fast
blocks.content: Move the pan down one rack and loosely cover it with foil for the remaining bake time.

blocks.alt: Focaccia wrapped in paper beside a reheated slice
blocks.caption: Keep the cooled bread covered at room temperature for up to two days.
blocks.credit: Synthetic fixture illustration generated for Cognis visual QA

blocks.content: Freeze sliced focaccia in an airtight container for up to one month. Reheat from thawed at **180 °C for 6–8 minutes**.

blocks.title: Allergens
blocks.content: Contains wheat (gluten). Check the yeast and any toppings for allergen cross-contact when serving guests.

blocks.title: Food safety
blocks.content: Wash tomatoes and herbs before use. Cool bread fully before sealing it, or trapped steam can encourage mold.
